name: מְרִיב בַּעַל
gloss: contender of the lord; or the lord contends
summary: The name Chronicles gives to Jonathan's son (1Ch 8:34; 9:40, once spelled מְרִי בַעַל), whom Samuel calls מְפִיבֹשֶׁת, Mephibosheth: lame in both feet from the day his nurse fled with him at the news of Saul and Jonathan's death (2Sa 4:4), to whom David showed kindness for Jonathan's sake and who ate at the king's table (2Sa 9:6–13). As with Eshbaal and Jerubbaal, Samuel's form puts בֹּשֶׁת “shame” for בַּעַל. The name is בַּעַל “lord” with a form of רִיב “contend”: one who contends, or whom the lord defends, as in Jerubbaal; scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “The son of Jonathan was מְרִיב בַּעַל, and Merib-baal begot Micah.”
The same, the second time written מְרִי בַעַל.
The same son of Jonathan, “lame in his feet … his name was מְפִיבֹשֶׁת”.
“Do not fear, for I will surely show you kindness for the sake of Jonathan your father.”
The other name of רִיב with בַּעַל, explained: “let Baal contend against him”.

note: Filed under בעל as no ריב entry exists; BDB files it under ריב (t.cm.al, with the spelling מְרִי בַעַל under m.dm.ac as a cross-reference). מְרִיב may be a participle-like noun “contender” (cf. Hos 4:4 כִמְרִיבֵי כֹהֵן) or the verb. TIPNR keys this Jonathan's son as Mephibosheth@2Sa.4.4; Saul's son Mephibosheth@2Sa.21.8 is another man, never called Merib-baal.
